sentences.text: Eretmosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur, a marine reptile meaning 'oar lizard', that lived during the Early and Middle Jurassic in England and Russia.
Two species of Eretmosaurus are known: E. rugosus and E. dubius.
Richard Owen first described the specimens of E. rugosus in 1840, originally naming them Plesiosaurus rugosus.
Harry Govier Seeley named Eretmosaurus rugosus in 1874 based on the headless skeleton specimen NHMUK 14435.
Brown and Bardet petitioned the ICZN in 1994 regarding the lost holotype, leading to NHMUK 14435 being designated the official neotype in 1996.
A fragmentary specimen of E. rugosus was identified from the Middle Jurassic of Siberia by Menner in 1992.
A partial skull and skeleton of E. dubius was discovered in the Harpoceras faleifer zone at Whitby, England, and initially described by Blake and Tate in 1876 as Plesiosaurus dubius.
The classification of Eretmosaurus has shifted over time, moving from Rhomaleosauridae to Pliosauridae, then Elasmosauridae, and most recently to Microcleididae.
Eretmosaurus lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
